## 1. The secure town  (`#the-secure-town`)

Cited ayat: 16:112-113

> **16:112** وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا قَرْيَةً كَانَتْ ءَامِنَةً مُّطْمَئِنَّةً يَأْتِيهَا رِزْقُهَا رَغَدًا مِّن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ ٱللَّهِ فَأَذَٰقَهَا ٱللَّهُ لِبَاسَ ٱلْجُوعِ وَٱلْخَوْفِ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَصْنَعُونَ
>
> **16:113** وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْهُمْ فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَهُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (16:112): God struck a similitude: a town that was secure and at ease, its provision coming to it in plenty from every place; it disbelieved in the favours of God, so God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear because of what they used to do.

**c2** (16:113): A messenger from among them had come to them and they called him a liar, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.

### One-minute summary

God struck a similitude of a town that was secure and at ease, with its provision coming in plenty from every place [c1]. It disbelieved in the favours of God, and God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear [c1].

### Complete story

God struck a similitude: a town that was secure and at ease, its provision coming to it in plenty from every place [c1]. It disbelieved in the favours of God, so God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear because of what they used to do [c1]. A messenger from among them had come to them and they called him a liar [c2]. The punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers [c2].

### Deep study

The first ayah describes the town as secure and supplied, and then at the point of hunger and fear [c1]. The next ayah says that a messenger from among them had come and was called a liar before the punishment seized them [c2]. The ayat do not name the town, the messenger or the punishment [c1][c2].

### Kids mode

God struck a similitude of a town that was secure and at ease, with its provision coming in plenty [c1]. The town disbelieved in the favours of God, and God made it taste hunger and fear [c1]. A messenger from among them had come, and they called him a liar [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set security and plenty beside disbelief in the favours of God, and then hunger and fear [c1]. Another reading is that the ayat link the seizing by the punishment with calling the messenger a liar [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which town is meant, where or when it was, or who the messenger was; none is named.
- Not established: whether the similitude describes a particular past town or is an example.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later commentary links the town to a particular place; this draft does not repeat or vouch for it.
- The verb kafarat in 16:112 can be read as disbelieved or as was ungrateful; this draft keeps disbelieved in the favours of God and leaves the sense open.
- The ayah itself says that God struck a similitude (mathal).
